Documents scoped multi-format image export and reference matching; broader professional qualification and multiple advanced capabilities remain open.
Historical receipt for manually authored and exported three-board menu document; does not prove local-agent autonomy or current release qualification.
Historical native manual composition/export receipt using an externally generated source; not RAW/log/offline/AI-agent proof.

Target platform mac-arm; commercialTermsApproved=false; price and checkout URLs blank. Do not advertise price, public availability, subscription-free terms, Intel, Windows or mobile support.

global_claim_caveats: No fastest, industry-leading, professional-grade accuracy, all-cameras, all-codecs or replacement-for-everything assertion.
No synthetic or stock image is described as an image generated or edited in Looksi without the matching product execution.
No offline, privacy, local-agent or zero-cloud claim is made without complete recorded proof for that run.

Time compression, dramatization and externally generated source art are identified wherever used.

campaigns.hook: I built this. I’d love your honest take.
campaigns.caption_instagram:
I built this. I’d love your honest take.

I’m building LOOKSi, a photo and video editor. The aim is useful control for professional projects, with room to explore when you make things for yourself.

I’ll be sharing real edits, the choices behind them, and what I’m still improving. What would make editing better for you?
campaigns.reddit_title: I’m building a photo and video editor. What should I put to the test?
campaigns.reddit_body:
I’m the person building LOOKSi, a photo and video editor. I’m trying to make something that gives working creatives useful control and gives hobbyists a place to grow.

For this first look I want to show one real edit, including a change of mind and the exported result. I’ll describe what is working in that build and where it still needs work.

If you edit photos, video, or both: what single workflow would you want me to demonstrate next? Tell me the kind of project and the awkward step, and I can make the next demo specific.
campaigns.cta: What would make it better for you?
founder_requirements: Required for full founder version: one seated A-roll take, 30–45 seconds; three opening takes.
Record quiet room sound and clean voice. Capture a 5-second listening/looking-at-screen cutaway.
No founder capture required for the text-led motion concept; do not use a synthetic founder likeness or voice.
demo_requirements: Own photo plus 2–3 own video clips; one current-build session showing actual edits and exports.
Keep uncut capture, build identity, source files and final outputs.
Do not reuse historical fixture screenshots as if the demo happened now.
campaigns.alt_text: A note from the builder: I built this. I’d love your honest take. An editor I’m building for people who care about photos and video. LOOKSi signature and additive RGB accents in an original typographic campaign design.

campaigns.reddit_title: What would make a photo/video editor worth testing in your workflow?
campaigns.reddit_body:
I’m building LOOKSi, and I’d like to put a concrete workflow in front of people who edit regularly.

My planned demonstration is one small project: a photo treatment, a short video cut, one deliberate revision, and the actual exports. I’ll retain the uncut session and list the build and source formats so the claims stay specific.

demo_requirements: Required for full demo: source photo and video footage from one owned project; current-build photo edit, timeline trim, one revision and exports.
Inspect outputs independently and retain metadata. Compare like-for-like framing, color profile and display conditions.
If timing is accelerated, label time compressed; never use an animation as performance proof.

campaigns.title: Start with your eye
campaigns.audience: Hobby photographers, occasional video makers and people learning to edit
campaigns.caption_instagram:
Your eye. Your first edit.

Pick a photo you like. Ask what you want someone to notice. Try one change, then compare.

That’s where I want the first LOOKSi walkthrough to begin. I’m building a photo and video editor for professional work and personal discovery. What part of editing feels confusing?
campaigns.reddit_title: What should a first photo-editing walkthrough explain?
campaigns.reddit_body:
I’m building LOOKSi, a photo and video editor, and I want the first walkthrough to be useful to people who do not edit every day.

My proposed starting point is one photo: choose what you want the viewer to notice, make one tonal change, compare it with the original, and export a version you like. Then we can build toward a short video edit.

If you are learning, what step needs the clearest explanation? If you teach editing, what do beginners usually get left to figure out alone?
campaigns.cta: What part of editing feels confusing?
founder_requirements: Optional: calm voiceover recorded in short sentences; a face-to-camera greeting can be added.
Use plain-language narration; name a control only after saying what visual choice it helps make.
demo_requirements: One owned everyday photograph with a clearly chosen subject; record original and actual adjusted output.
Capture one real control change, matched comparison, export, and independent open of the output.
The tutorial is photo-first. Mention video as the product scope without implying the photo walkthrough teaches video.
campaigns.alt_text: Start with your eye: Your eye. Your first edit. A little curiosity goes a long way. Let’s make something you like. LOOKSi signature and additive RGB accents in an original typographic campaign design.

campaigns.caption_instagram:
final_final_actuallyfinal.

If you know, you know.

I’m building LOOKSi, a photo and video editor, and I know the feeling of an edit growing another ‘final’ version. This is a joke about the process we all recognize.

Tell me your most chaotic file name.
campaigns.reddit_title: What is your most chaotic final-final file name?
campaigns.reddit_body:
I’m building a photo and video editor called LOOKSi, and the editing habit behind this little campaign idea felt familiar: final, final_final, final_final_actuallyfinal.

The graphic is a joke about our process, not a demonstration of automatic version management or a claim that the tool fixes it.

What is your most chaotic file name, and what were you still changing? I’m the builder and would like to understand the actual revision decisions behind the joke.
campaigns.cta: Tell me your most chaotic file name.
founder_requirements: Optional 10-minute skit: satisfied glance, doubtful glance, return to screen; three 3-second shots.

demo_requirements: Text-only skit needs no UI footage and makes no feature demonstration claim.
If product footage is inserted: record an actual warming/cooling adjustment and undo on the same owned source; retain the session.
Frame behavior as a dramatized editing habit, not as a testimonial from an actual customer.

campaigns.caption_instagram:
It starts with how you see.

A frame. A feeling. A point of view.

I’m building LOOKSi, a photo and video editor, around the choices that make the work yours. For professional projects and for the things you make because you want to.

Follow the build.
campaigns.reddit_title: What makes an editing tool feel like it belongs in your creative process?
campaigns.reddit_body:
I’m building LOOKSi, a photo and video editor. The question behind it is personal: can the tool give deliberate choices room, from a photograph to a cut?

The visual direction for this introduction uses light, rhythm and restrained typography. The product demonstrations will show real source-to-export decisions separately so the mood film does not stand in for proof.

What makes a tool feel like it belongs in your creative process: the way it lets you explore, the way it lets you finish, or something else?
founder_requirements: Optional clean voiceover with space between sentences; no face-to-camera requirement.
A founder voice can anchor the I’m building line. Do not synthesize the founder’s voice.
demo_requirements: No app footage is required for the abstract brand-film version; label it as brand motion in production records.
If a finished photo/video is added, identify its source and authorship accurately.
The film does not substantiate product usability, processing quality, performance or release readiness.
